subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What different kinds of hardware problems appear in these incidents?

judge.implied_focus: The type/category of hardware problem (and affected component) present in each incident

per_column.name: hardware_problem_type
per_column.rationale: Directly categorizes the kind of hardware fault (Printer, Power/Boot Failure, Overheating, etc.), which is precisely what the query asks about.

per_column.name: hardware_component
per_column.rationale: Identifies the physical component affected, a coherent complementary facet of the same hardware-problem focus, adding a device/part granularity.

judge.rationale: Both columns centre tightly on ONE inferable focus -- classifying hardware problems in the incidents -- so focus coherence is high. The implied focus is actionable: an analyst can quantify problem types, spot that printers dominate, and target remediation. Structure quality is only moderate because the two columns are highly redundant: their value distributions are nearly identical (Printer 83, Monitor 28, Keyboard 24, Mouse 7...), so 'component' largely restates 'problem_type' rather than providing an orthogonal facet (e.g., failure mode, severity, root cause). The pair leans toward a single-restatement rather than a differentiated multi-facet structure. The pervasive NULLs (418) reflect non-hardware incidents and are acceptable given the query scope, but the near-duplication of the two columns limits the analytical richness of the decomposition.
